title: Abaxent: explaining what a broker does
summaryLead: A website for a technology broker that has to explain what a broker is.
story: Abaxent is a Wisconsin technology broker that has been at it for 22 years. It works with every major vendor but represents the buyer, which isn't what people expect from someone selling technology, and the old site didn't make that clear. They wanted visitors to get it quickly and to reach the leadership team without hunting. So we started the site with one question, what is a technology broker, and let the rest answer it: how a deal works, the numbers behind it, past projects and certifications.

features.title: Scroll-driven video hero
features.text: The film starts in a frame and opens to full width as you scroll.
features.alt: Abaxent hero: Technology brokers. Not vendors.
features.story: We wanted a film on the first screen without slowing the page down. The video and its poster frame live inside the page, so there's no extra request, and it stops playing for anyone who has reduced motion turned on.

features.title: Four-step method
features.text: How a broker works, drawn as a four-step pyramid.
features.alt: How a technology broker works, with the pyramid graphic
features.story: A broker is hard to picture, so we drew one. The pyramid is a single SVG shape recolored in CSS, which keeps it sharp at any size and means there's no image to load.

features.title: Impact numbers
features.text: 22 years, 93% partner retention, 75+ partners and 3.2x economic impact, right up front.

features.title: Leadership
features.text: Portraits, short bios and direct lines for the three leaders.

features.title: Why we're different
features.text: Four short reasons in plain language: brokers not vendors, no bench, 22 years, certified.
